steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Such a sound... do not fear, child.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Matriarch.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You too, Nurturer. Thank you for your work.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I simply did what I could.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The child is still weak. Take him back to his mother, Andoain.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I will come and find you.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: You seem unwell, Matriarch. Should I escort you to your apartments?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I am fine. The heartbeat continues to echo within me.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Not just the mother. I can hear countless hearts resonating, so powerful it seems they could bring down this shrine.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The people have begun to link with one another, irrespective of race or background... but some have rejected the future we revealed.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The Nativity has come to an end. Our kindred need not stay here. We should prepare for the next stage.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Understood. You should retire. I will take care of the rest.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Once again, welcome to the Shrine of Nurtury.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Whether you understood the Matriarch's proposal at the summit, and regardless of what you think of it, the birth and enlightenment of this arborbeast is undoubtedly a clear revelation.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: On how to remove the barriers between nations and races... on how to resolve hatred and build lasting peace... on facing the calamity that hangs over our heads together.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Beginning with the Nativity, the second Summit of Nations now enters a new stage—

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Laterano will share our halo with all races!

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: 'May our Lord share the blessings with all.'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Fiammetta! Mostima! Over here!

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Lemuel?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: When did you come back? Why didn't you tell us?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Nice outfit, huh? Including those handcuffs...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I wanted to surprise you. Well... hee hee.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: (Scratches head)

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What happened, Lemuen?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: ...It's a long story.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I could buy you two minutes, if you want to make a break for it.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Sure—

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: On second thought, maybe next time. I've caused enough trouble for my sister already.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Did I interrupt a reunion?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Velliv.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Can you take the suspect to the Seventh Tribunal on your own, Cardinal Lemuen?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Or do you need support? After all, attempted sabotage of the Shrine of Nurtury and Summit of Nations is a serious charge.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: If you're concerned, you are free to come with us, or have a gun-knight keep watch.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Don't talk like that. After all, according to your conclavist Cardinal Aide Amos's testimony, you picked up Lemuel's trail at another scene beforehand...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Are you saying I tried to cover for my sister?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Well, not exactly. All the evidence is circumstantial, and there is nothing that proves you did anything wrong.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Do you recall our previous conversation in the Shrine?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: I admire your ability and resolve greatly, Lemuen the Silent. But I also know when these virtues of yours are most prominently displayed.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Besides, it's natural for us to be cautious when your sister is involved. I hope you understand.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: No need to worry. Letting El run around with all these charges against her won't help her.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Of course. I'm sure the misunderstanding can be resolved, as long as Lemuel cooperates.

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: One moment, Shimmering Vigil... and Legatus Mostima.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Velliv
steps.text: Please remain here at the Shrine of Nurtury. The Curia has a mission for you.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: They... took El away?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: After all the effort it took for Magister to get me off the hook...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Come on, Vani... isn't there anything else you can do?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Don't bother knocking, Andoain. I have nothing to hide from you.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The mother?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Sleeping.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I brought the child. His feathers are not yet grown in, but he is surprisingly lively. I thought perhaps you might want to pet him again.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Thank you. It is comforting to me.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: This place...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Do you remember? We built it to house the mother when we came to Laterano. It became the first nursery of the shrine.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I remember. We made this simple yet warm bed together, and hung the comfort bells that gave her restful sleep.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The room is no longer in use, but I come back from time to time, if only for prayer.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: This was our starting point, yours and mine.

steps.name: Arborbeast
steps.text: (Stretches happily)

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I sense that he likes this place too.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: His halo is so bright. I noticed it the moment you brought him here.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: It is the miracle that you have long believed in.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But I don't understand. What brought on the premonitions of the miracle when you first encountered the mother?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I had no premonitions, Andoain, I only saw your struggling heart.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: She was on her last legs, and what she needed was not healing, but her last rites. Yet you wanted to save her, and you would not allow the idea to be dispelled by common sense.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I believed that this thought, which you protected so dearly, could create the miracle of life.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Life is a wonderful thing, one that can never be measured by the confines of common sense.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Anyone would want to save her, Matriarch.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Therefore, anyone can create miracles. Miracles are so because people do not believe in the power of faith.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Is it the halo that gives Sankta faith, or faith that gives Sankta the halo? Have you ever pondered it?

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Our Law, empathy, and firearms, and the Paradise that we built atop them...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Did they all arise from a blessing without a cause, as common sense would indicate?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: ...I don't know.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The past has its beginnings, as does the future.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: The Shrine of Nurtury... This towering edifice was not built in a day. It began as a simple, ordinary nursery.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Our nursery...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Did we start with the blueprints of such an imposing shrine? No. We merely wished for a safe, comfortable room for that mother...

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: And yet, its frenzied evolution led to what it is now.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: That is how a future where all are saved can sprout from our faith.

spans.text: is how a future where all are saved can sprout from our faith.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Matriarch... I followed you because I had long searched for such a future, and you happened to know the way.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But I never thought, nor could I comprehend, why you believed it could begin with me.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What I'm able to do is, ultimately, insignificant.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Insignificant trifles and grandiose feats are but a hair's breadth from one another. You have labored for many years over this grueling journey of yours. You should not let such a meaningless difference stay your steps.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I will need you to lift your spirits, for aside from caring for this mother and child, there are more deeds that must be done... such as the next Nativity.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You're early.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I'm already packed. You can just stick the seals on top so I can go back to bed.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Patrizion?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Hmph. I thought you were him.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I was told the last part of the handover would be handled by the Notarial Hall. Why did they send gun-knights?

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: That was assuming nothing had been tampered with.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: What are you talking about?

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Both the storage room and equipment show signs of recent use.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Cardinal Aide Amos must have made it clear when he last came here—

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: All gunsmithing operations were to cease immediately upon signing the papers. Any unauthorized work on patron firearms or explosives would be a violation of law.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I've had this little workshop for decades. I couldn't let it go so easily...

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I just wanted to hear these old boys move again one last time and shed some tears over it. Is that so wrong?

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: You've already said as much.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Your apprentice, Vannini, the one you took with you from the Shrine of Nurtury—where is she?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Must've gone back to watch the Nativity.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: She's not a kid anymore. Besides, I don't see so well. Can't keep an eye on her all the time.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: In that case, let us continue this conversation somewhere else.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: What if I don't want to?

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: I do not wish to resort to force, unless absolutely necessary.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: It was Patrizion who sent you here, wasn't it?

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Come with me.

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: S-Sister Hildegard, Reverend Gun-Knight?

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Is she not in the monastery?

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: Y-Yes, but... she just had an accident. She's resting now.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: It's hard to explain...

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: A mobile confessional suddenly showed up at the monastery yesterday. Sister Hildegard was lying inside, unconscious...

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: There was no one else; someone had set the confessional's navigation system to bring her here. We're not sure what happened to her.

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: Perhaps we can have her report to you once she wakes up.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: This is urgent. Bring me to her.

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... It's alright, Sister Gerain.

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: Hildegard! You're awake? The porridge...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I'm fine, just a little dizzy.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I ate the porridge on the table. I'm coughing because some of it went down the wrong pipe.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Reverend Gun-Knight, you came for Arturia, didn't you?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Yes, it's true that Arturia left Landen Monastery without permission...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: But I went after her as soon as I found out! And I caught her! But something unexpected happened...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Please, give Landen Monastery a little more time... no, give me a little more time.

spans.text: Please, give Landen Monastery a little more time... no, give

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: We would like you to come with us, Sister Hildegard.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Well... alright.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: It would be best if you came too, Sister.

steps.name: Nervous Nun
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Sister Gerain doesn't have anything to do with this.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I was the one in charge of supervising Arturia. This is my fault...

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: No need to worry, Sister Hildegard.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: With a major incident like this, the Curia needs as much information as we can get.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Now, follow me, please.
